correctness.rationale: In a regular \(p\)-group the elements killed by \(p\) form \(\Omega_1(G)\), so exponent greater than \(p\) forces \(\Omega_1(G)\ne G\); the published 2020 theorem then gives exactly the displayed bound and equality criterion. For \(n\le p\), class at most \(n-1<p\) invokes Hall regularity. For \(C_p\wr C_p=C_p^p\rtimes C_p\), direct multiplication shows an element outside the base has order \(p\) exactly when its coordinate sum is zero and otherwise order \(p^2\); counting generators of cyclic subgroups yields the stated formula and excess. The two order-\(p\) standard generators also show \(\Omega_1(W)=W\).

value.rationale: This resolves a natural initial range of a published second-maximum problem for every odd prime and proves that the boundary \(n=p\) is intrinsic by an explicit next-order exception. That is a meaningful structural cutoff, not an arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: The global problem from order \(p^{p+1}\) onward remains open.

final_claim: For every odd prime \(p\) and \(n\ge3\), the second cyclic-subgroup maximum among regular groups of order \(p^n\) is \(M_{p,n}=(2p^{n-1}-p^{n-2}+p-2)/(p-1)\), with equality exactly at exponent \(p^2\) and \([G:\Omega_1(G)]=p\). Hence this is the global second maximum for \(3\le n\le p\), and the cutoff is sharp because \(C_p\wr C_p\) at order \(p^{p+1}\) exceeds \(M_{p,p+1}\) by \(p^{p-2}(p-1)\).
limitations: The theorem does not determine the global second maximum for \(n\ge p+1\).
The wreath product is a strict lower-bound witness at the first exceptional order, not claimed extremal there.
